title: Momentum cadence release logbook
content:
Purpose
This logbook captures a compact, operational view of a release cycle designed for high-frequency, low-friction feature ramps. It combines a lightweight roadmap slice, target KPIs, cohorted rollout plan, and a single-page readiness checklist with explicit triggers and owners. Use this during weekly product-ops syncs and the final go/no-go decision meeting.

Summary / scope
Feature: Adaptive batching suggestions (server-side)
Goal: Reduce median token cost by 12% for chat-heavy customers while keeping p95 latency under 350ms on hosted tiers.
Release window: staggered 6-week ramp (canary -> phased cohorts -> 100%)
Primary stakeholders: Product (Leah Kim), Eng (Jamal Ortiz), SRE (Oscar Rivera), Solutions Eng (Ariana Patel)

Roadmap tracker (snapshot)
- Week 0 (2025-09-22 to 2025-09-28): Spec approved, integration spikes completed, canary infra reserved. Owner: Product.
- Week 1: Canary build deployed to 2% of traffic (internal + pilot customers). Observe latency, cost, correctness. Owner: Eng.
- Week 2: Canary metrics review; adjust kernel selection and batching thresholds; enable auto-fallback. Owner: Eng/SRE.
- Week 3: Start phased cohort A (10% traffic, mix of PLG and paid). Monitor hypothesis KPIs. Owner: Product Ops.
- Week 4: If KPIs stable, expand Cohort B (40%); otherwise, pause & remediate. Owner: Product.
- Week 5: Full rollout (100%) or rollback. Owner: Leadership.

KPI definitions & target thresholds (primary + guardrails)
Primary KPIs (decision-driving):
- Unit cost delta (token-cost-per-response): target -12% median vs baseline; action if > -6%
- P95 latency (end-to-end observed): target < 350ms; abort rollout if > 420ms sustained 15m
- Quality regressions (semantic score on eval prompt set): target <= 1% absolute regression; investigate if > 0.5%

Operational guardrails (safety net):
- Error rate (5xx) delta: must not increase by >0.25 percentage points across cohorts
- Request timeout fraction: should remain <0.5%
- Customer complaints (support tickets mentioning "generation quality" or "latency"): 0 per pilot cohort; if >=1 for a major customer, pause cohort expansion

Telemetry & dashboards (quick links)
- Live dashboard: product-ops/metrics/adaptive-batching (shows cost, latency percentiles, error rate by cohort)
- Tracing view: jaeger/adaptive-batching-canary
- Cost projection sheet: finance/optimize/ab-cost-forecast-Q4 (linked)_

Cohort rollout plan (explicit groups + timing)
- Canary (2%): internal + 3 pilot customers selected for low-latency tolerance. Duration: 72 hours steady-state.
- Cohort A (10%): mixed accounts, include 5 engaged customers (SE-assisted). Duration: 7 days.
- Cohort B (40%): wider mix including mid-market customers. Duration: 7 days.
- Ramp to 100%: conditional on green signals.

Escalation triggers & immediate actions
- If P95 latency > 420ms sustained for 15 minutes: disable adaptive batching (automated fallback) and page SRE.
- If unit cost delta moves in wrong direction (+ >2% cost): revert batching config to prior baseline and queue hotfix.
- If semantic eval regression > 1%: freeze rollout and open "quality-triage" war room with research and eng.
- If critical customer files ticket or SLA alert: pause expansion and run customer-specific rollback.

Pre-launch readiness checklist (must be GREEN before cohort A)
- [ ] Spec doc finalized and reviewed (Confluence link in artifacts) — owner: Product
- [ ] Canary infra reservation validated for GPU pools (2x redundancy) — owner: Infra
- [ ] Observability hooks with tagging by cohort inserted, verified on synthetic traffic — owner: Observability
- [ ] Cost simulation run against last 30 days of traffic patterns — owner: Finance/Optimize
- [ ] SLO update drafted with rollback windows and customer notification templates — owner: Customer Success
- [ ] SE onboarding notes prepared for pilot customers (runbooks + QA checklist) — owner: Solutions Eng
- [ ] Incident runbook with playbook steps and page targets — owner: SRE

Post-launch monitoring & cadence
- Daily first-week touchpoints: 09:30 AM product-ops standup with representatives from Eng, SRE, CS.
- Rolling 24/7 watch for first 72 hours with on-call SRE rotation.
- Weekly KPI sync: consolidate cohort metrics and recommend next action (expand, hold, rollback).

Runbook snippets (copyable)
- Automated fallback command: \"rampctl set-batching off --global\" (requires infra review, logged as automated mitigation).
- Quick rollback: deploy previous config tag (v1.17.3) to serving pools; expected failover < 6 minutes.

Open questions / risks (to surface during go/no-go)
- How sensitive are legacy quantized kernels to the new batching heuristics? (Research owns a short test matrix)
- Edge-case prompt patterns where batching introduces hallucination-like artifacts — need expanded eval set.
- Customer communication cadence for those on early cohorts (do we push targeted emails or SE outreach?).

Owner responsibilities (single line owners for fast comms)
- Product decisions & stakeholder comms: Leah Kim
- Engineering delivery & config rollouts: Jamal Ortiz
- Reliability & infra capacity: Oscar Rivera
- Customer outreach + pilot coordination: Ariana Patel

Decision rubric (fast yes/no)
- Go to cohort A if: Canary ran 72 hours with P95 < 350ms and unit cost delta <= -8% and no semantic regression >0.5%
- Hold if: mixed signals or missing telemetry — wait one full weekday and re-evaluate
- Abort if: any primary KPI breach (see KPI thresholds) or a critical ticket from a top-10 customer

Notes for retro (post 100% or rollback)
- Capture cost delta by customer cohort (to identify negative outliers)
- Timeline of mitigations and how long each took to restore
- Gaps in traces/observability that delayed diagnosis (action item for Observability team)

Quick action items (next 7 days)
- Run the canary synthetic suite against the new batching config (Jamal) — due: 2025-09-25
- Draft external-facing pilot note + SE scripts (Ariana) — due: 2025-09-27
- Finalize cost forecast and update console counters (Finance & Product Ops) — due: 2025-09-26

Appendix: minimal metric collection plan (for engineering)
- Tag each request with header: X-Rollout-Cohort and persist in traces
- Emit metrics: batching.enabled (bool), batching.batch_size_histogram, kv-cache-hit-rate, model-kernel-selected (string)
- Export daily aggregated snapshot to product-ops S3 bucket for retrospective analysis

--
Notes: This is intentionally concise. The goal is to reduce meeting friction and provide unequivocal thresholds for fast operational decisions during the ramp. Keep this doc updated with coordinator notes during the rollout (timestamped lines and brief decisions).
